_README: MARKER-ONLY. Never fetched by the student's browser until a teacher/marker PDF is generated (formative: automatically when the student clicks Generate; assessed: only via the ?teacher=1-gated action, after Final Submit). Never render any of this on the student-facing page. See CLAUDE.md §5's assessment-security amendment.

markingScheme.criterion: Accurately describes the pattern across at least two of their own forged stars at clearly different masses, quoting actual recorded figures for surface temperature, luminosity and H-R diagram position (hotter, more luminous, further up-left as mass rises).
markingScheme.accept: Any two genuine trials from the student's own Investigation Record showing the trend; approximate figures are fine, and 'luminosity scales roughly with mass^3.5' is not required if the direction and scale of the change is captured.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim ('bigger stars are hotter') with no actual recorded temperature/luminosity figures quoted from at least two of their own stars.

markingScheme.criterion: States clearly whether the evidence supported or refuted the hypothesis chosen before forging, explicitly referencing their own recorded data.
markingScheme.accept: Any judgement (supported / refuted / partially supported) that is consistent with what their own data actually shows and refers back to it.
markingScheme.insufficient: Repeating the hypothesis wording without saying whether the evidence agreed with it.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains, in terms of gravity and nuclear fusion rate, why a much more massive star has a dramatically shorter main-sequence lifespan despite starting with more fuel (greater mass compresses the core more strongly, driving a much faster fusion rate, so the extra fuel is burned through far faster than it lasts).
markingScheme.accept: Equivalent scientific wording; the specific scaling exponents (mass^3.5, mass^-2.5) are not required if the compression-drives-faster-fusion mechanism is clearly stated.
markingScheme.insufficient: Stating only that 'it runs out of fuel faster' without linking this to gravity compressing the core and speeding up fusion.

markingScheme.criterion: Gives one specific, correct difference for a 20 M☉ Sun — either it would be far hotter/more luminous (higher up the H-R diagram) or it would have a dramatically shorter main-sequence lifespan (millions, not billions, of years) — linked to a mechanism (greater mass compresses the core more, driving much faster fusion).
markingScheme.accept: Either the temperature/luminosity/H-R difference or the lifespan difference counts for this point, as long as a mechanism is given.
markingScheme.insufficient: Stating a difference with no mechanism at all ('it would be different').

markingScheme.criterion: Gives a second, genuinely distinct difference from the first (not a restatement) — most clearly that a 20 M☉ star would end its life as a supernova and a neutron star or black hole, rather than a red giant and a gentle white dwarf — again linked to a mechanism.
markingScheme.accept: Any second difference that is mechanism-based and clearly distinct in kind from the first (e.g. if the first point was about temperature/luminosity, this one should be about lifespan or fate, not the same idea reworded).
markingScheme.insufficient: A second sentence that just restates the first difference in other words (e.g. 'it would also be hotter').

markingScheme.criterion: Finishes with a genuine evaluation sentence stating a confidence level in their own conclusion AND naming one specific, plausible way to make the investigation more reliable (e.g. more repeat trials per mass band, comparing the model's numbers to real catalogued stars).
markingScheme.insufficient: A vague 'I am confident in my answer' with no named way to improve reliability.

criteria.source: Auto-marked from the Knowledge Check (auto_marked_score, kc1-kc4; kc5 is an unscored reflection slider) — the teacher does not mark this row.
= the Explain question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one (data pattern across two stars, hypothesis judgement, fusion-rate mechanism). Do not award these 3 marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: No use of own forged-star data, or the hypothesis is never addressed.
Describes temperature and/or luminosity increasing with mass in general terms, but does not quote own recorded figures or does not check against the chosen hypothesis.
Quotes own recorded figures for at least two stars and checks against the hypothesis, but the explanation of why lifespan falls so sharply with mass is incomplete.

Quotes specific recorded figures from at least two stars of clearly different mass, clearly states whether this supported or refuted the chosen hypothesis, and correctly explains that greater mass drives faster core fusion, cutting lifespan far more than the extra fuel extends it.

criteria.source: = the Apply question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one (first difference+mechanism, second distinct difference+mechanism, evaluation sentence). Do not award these 3 marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: No credible difference given for a 20-solar-mass Sun, or differences are not linked to a pattern observed in the Forge.
Gives one plausible difference (temperature, luminosity, lifespan or fate) linked to a Forge observation, but the second is missing or unlinked.
Gives two plausible differences each linked to a Forge observation, but the closing evaluation sentence (confidence plus a way to improve reliability) is missing or vague.

Gives two specific, correct differences (for example hotter/more luminous, and a supernova/neutron-star or black-hole fate instead of a white dwarf), each clearly linked to a pattern observed in the Forge, plus a genuine evaluation sentence naming a confidence level and one specific way to make the investigation more reliable.

criteria.source: Assessed holistically across both the Explain and Apply answers together — independent of, and never overlapping with, the content marks in use_of_evidence and reasoning above.

levels.descriptor: Hard to follow, or astronomy terms are missing or used incorrectly.
Understandable, but with unclear phrasing or a misused term (for example confusing mass and weight, or luminosity and brightness-as-seen-from-Earth).
Clear, well-formed sentences using correct astronomy vocabulary (mass, luminosity, fusion, H-R diagram, spectral class) throughout.

markingInstructions: Mark ONLY the two constructed responses (Explain, Apply). Award marks point-by-point using each question's marking_scheme in marking_context: each point is worth the marks stated, is independent unless it names a dependsOn point (in which case only award it if that earlier point was also awarded), and each point's 'accept'/'insufficient' tell you exactly what does and doesn't count. use_of_evidence's 3 marks ARE the Explain marking_scheme's 3 points, and reasoning's 3 marks ARE the Apply marking_scheme's 3 points — the rubric levels restate the same points as bands; award each set of 3 marks ONCE, not twice. communication is a separate, holistic 2 marks across both answers' clarity and vocabulary, never overlapping with the content marks. The Knowledge Check is already auto-marked in auto_marked_score (kc1-kc4; kc5 is an unscored reflection slider) — copy it into knowledge_accuracy (6 marks = full). Use the student's actual logged stars (the mass/spectralClass/tempK/luminosity/lifespan/fate columns in simulation_results.trials) to verify any figure they claim to quote — do not take their prose summary on trust if it does not match their own logged data. Accept scientifically valid alternative wording per each point's 'accept' field, and do not penalise spelling unless meaning is unclear. Total is out of 14 (6 auto + 3 + 3 + 2); report the percentage, one strength, one correction, and one next step, in under 80 words.
